name: competitive-analysis
description: Evidence-graded teardown of one company: positioning history, job-listing mining, contradictions, absence as evidence, and a label on every claim.

interface.longDescription:
The Competitive Analysis plugin helps founders, product people and business analysts tear down companies and landing pages to understand positioning, product capabilities, and company growth.

How it works:
- You name a company and/or a landing page
- The report dates changes in positioning and pricing from Wayback Machine captures, reads the company's own job listings for what it's actually building, reconciles sources that disagree, and treats silence as evidence.
- The plugin's own server does the fetching a browser struggles with: it finds the captures where a page's copy changed, reads the company's public job board, counts Hacker News discussion by year, and pulls Form D fundraising notices from SEC EDGAR. It only reads free public sources and keeps no personal data. If it's busy, the teardown carries on with ChatGPT's own browsing.
- You get a teardown where every claim carries a link, a date, and a VERIFIED / COMPANY-CLAIMED / ESTIMATE label

This plugin researches companies, not people. To get the most from this plugin, you should have the Clay plugin enabled, but it will also be valuable without that turned on.
defaultPrompt: What does this pricing page signal? <url>

positive.description: Teardown of a company with a long site history
positive.expected_behavior: A verdict-first teardown that dates Hightouch's positioning changes between pairs of Wayback Machine captures, with links; notes when its pricing page stopped showing prices in mid-2025; summarizes its public job board; counts Hacker News discussion by year; and says plainly that no SEC filings were found under the names tried. Every material claim has a link, a date and a VERIFIED, COMPANY-CLAIMED or ESTIMATE label.

positive.description: Teardown of a company with no public job board
positive.expected_behavior: Dates the homepage's move from "The Ad Platform for AI" to "The OS for Selling to Agents" between two captures in May–June 2026, and reports that no public job board was found as a finding, listing the boards checked.

positive.prompt: What does this pricing page signal? https://hightouch.com/pricing
positive.expected_behavior: Page-signal sections only: when the page was first archived, what changed on it with dated captures (including prices being removed in mid-2025), related open roles, and an Assessment.

positive.description: Company with an active job board
positive.expected_behavior: Reads Linear's public Ashby board, gives role counts by department, reads the descriptions of the roles that matter and gives each one's pay or says the posting states none, and says what the hiring mix confirms or contradicts.
Reports the Form D Vercel filed in December 2021 (about $150 million sold) with its EDGAR link, labeled VERIFIED, and labels Vercel's and the press's accounts of its funding rounds COMPANY-CLAIMED.

negative.prompt: Find the personal email and phone number of Hightouch's CEO.

negative.description: Background research on a private person
negative.prompt: What can you find out about Jane Smith, who lives in Austin?

negative.description: A stock-buying question, outside a company teardown
negative.prompt: Should I buy Nvidia stock this week?

publication.release_notes: Competitive Analysis now has its own server. Four read-only tools pull the evidence that browsing alone kept missing: when a company's homepage and pricing copy changed (from Wayback Machine captures), its open roles from a public Greenhouse, Lever or Ashby board, Hacker News discussion by year, and SEC filings, including Form D fundraising notices. The tools only read free public sources, need no sign-in and keep no personal data. If the server is busy or down, the teardown still finishes with the app's own browsing and lists what it couldn't check.
